findings.title: Part 1b text says Change folder… is refused only while a recording or export runs
findings.body: This PR makes a group move lock the switch and the relocate path too: `busy` now comes from `activeTransactionDeps()` (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts:346-347`), `relocateFolder` spreads that object (`index.ts:480`), and `relocate.ts:24-25` returns `{ reason: busy }`, which can be `"moving"` (`shared/types/workspaces.ts:25`). The renderer already has the `moving` copy (`relocate-copy.ts:35-36`, `en.json:2630`). The sentence at lines 25-27 still lists only "while a recording or export runs". Suggest adding "or a group move" there, matching the spec's relocate row.

findings.title: IPC table: workspaces:relocate refusals omit the group-move lock
findings.body: The `workspaces:relocate` row ends with "and while a recording or export runs". The code also refuses with `reason: "moving"` during a group move (`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/relocate.ts:24-25` via the shared `busy()` at `index.ts:346-347`, re-checked after the picker at `relocate.ts:33`). Add "or a group move" to the list so the channel contract matches `WorkspaceRelocateRefusal` (`shared/types/workspaces.ts:157-158`). I read this table and grepped the rest of the spec for the relocate wording; no other place says this.

findings.title: The new "moving" refusal has no test
findings.body: `explains each remaining refusal` lists every other `WorkspaceRelocateRefusal` reason, but not `moving`. The string `relocateMoving` appears only in `relocate-copy.ts:35-36` (grep over the feature folder found no other reference), so a wrong key or a dropped case would pass. Add `[{ ok: false, reason: "moving" }, /Wait for the move to finish/]` to the list. The main-side `relocate.test.ts:170-185` and `:247-271` also cover only recording and exporting, so the `moving` branch of `busy` is not tested there either (that file is outside this part).

contracts.action: Change folder… (relocate) while a group move runs
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts:363-368 (runSwitch uses the same activeTransactionDeps busy check)
contracts.before_after: busy was only in runSwitch's own object (removed at old index.ts:367); it now lives in activeTransactionDeps (index.ts:346-347), which both runSwitch (index.ts:363) and relocateFolder (index.ts:480) spread. Relocate is refused with reason moving before the picker opens (relocate.ts:33) and checked again after it.
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog shows "Wait for the move to finish before changing a workspace's folder." (relocate-copy.ts:35-36, en.json:2630).
contracts.failure_mode: If the move throws, the finally clears moveRun and re-broadcasts state (index.ts:218-222), so the lock is released and the next relocate is not refused.

contracts.action: Switch to another workspace while a group move runs
contracts.before_after: busyNow() returns "moving" while moveRun is set (index.ts:66-68), and moveRun is set at index.ts:166. The switch refusal reason "moving" is in WorkspaceSwitchRefusal (shared/types/workspaces.ts:32-33).
contracts.visible_effect: The switcher is locked with "Wait for the move to finish to switch" (en.json:2635, existing key). I did not read the renderer that picks this key.
contracts.failure_mode: Open: a switch that passed its busy check before moveRun was set could overlap the start of a move. I did not read gate.ts to see whether gate.run refuses that case.
contracts.open_question: Can a switch that has already passed its busy check (switch-transaction.ts:50-51) run while moveItems sets moveRun (index.ts:166) and enters workspaceGate().run? Does the gate reject that overlap?

contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts:302 for recording and exporting (busyNow via host.busy())
contracts.before_after: listState now reports "moving" for the duration of a move (busyNow, index.ts:66-68). broadcastState runs when the move starts (index.ts:167) and in the finally (index.ts:221).
contracts.visible_effect: Renderer locks the switcher and Move-to menus from WorkspacesState.busy (shared/types/workspaces.ts:69-70). I did not read the renderer consumer.
contracts.failure_mode: A move that throws still reaches the finally, which re-broadcasts the state, so the lock clears. Whether the renderer re-renders from that broadcast is not checked.
contracts.open_question: Does the renderer's workspace state take the broadcast's busy value and clear the lock when it is null?

contracts.action: Change folder… on an empty or plain folder (not-a-workspace)
contracts.before_after: The case returns the relocateNotWorkspace string, which is now defined in en.json:2623 and es.json:2623 with the same key. The refusal happens before any write (relocate.ts is the check).
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog shows the alert (workspace-dialog.tsx:153). The test workspace-dialog.test.tsx:288-297 asserts the "a workspace folder that was moved" and "Move to" text.
contracts.failure_mode: None: the refusal changes nothing, and the alert stays until the next action.

thread_replies.reply: Addressed. A thrown group move now goes through refusalOfError (index.ts:215-217), so StaleWorkspaceError maps to stale, MaintenanceError to maintenance, and anything else to io.
Addressed. A rejected loadDeviceId clears the cached promise (index.ts:174-177), so the next group move asks again.

Addressed. The comment on skipped now says only Stop fills it, and a group refused as a whole lists its items in failed and leaves skipped empty (shared/types/workspaces.ts:252-256). The code matches that.
Addressed. chipLabel (es.json:2639), newWorkspace (es.json:2645) and reason_stale (es.json:2685) now say "espacio de trabajo", the same term as the rest of the file.

structuredOutput.summary: Reviewed the 8 files of part 1. No blocker or fix. The group-move busy lock now flows through activeTransactionDeps to both the switch and relocate paths, which is correct (index.ts:346-347, 363, 480; relocate.ts:24-25, 33). Findings are two docs items and one test gap, all "consider": the backlog doc (line 26) and the spec relocate row (line 1302) still say relocate is refused only while a recording or export runs, and the dialog test's refusal list has no "moving" case. Four open review threads on these files are addressed in the current code. Two open contracts remain: whether a switch can overlap the start of a move (gate.ts not read), and whether the renderer clears the lock from the list broadcast (renderer consumer not read). For the spec, I read the IPC table region in full and grepped the rest for the relocate wording, not the whole 1,300-line file.

findings.title: Part 1b text says Change folder… is refused only while a recording or export runs

The main-side `relocate.test.ts:170-185` and `:247-271` also cover only recording and exporting, so the `moving` branch of `busy` is not tested there either (that file is outside this part).
